title: Add benchmark-lab performance suites, profiling baselines and reporting pipeline (v140)
author: Maya Patel
description:
Motivation: expand the benchmark-lab coverage to include updated performance test suites, new profiling baselines for common model families, representative workload runners, and an end-to-end reporting pipeline that uploads aggregated results to the analytics warehouse. This PR bundles changes required to run v140 of the benchmark lab and to surface consistent metrics for cost/latency regression detection.

What changed (high level): added text-generation and embedding performance suites tuned for variable sequence lengths; introduced representative workload runners that simulate real customer distributions (chat, completions, embeddings, reranking); added profiling baselines and a harness for cold-start and steady-state memory/latency profiles; implemented a reporting pipeline that publishes summarized results to BigQuery and triggers downstream dashboards.

Checklist:
- [x] Add performance suites for text-generation and embeddings
- [x] Add representative runners and input distributions
- [x] Add profiling baseline artifacts and CI profile checks
- [x] Add reporting pipeline job + docs and alerting
- [x] Update CI workflow to run nightly benchmarks and profile checks

Backward compatibility: all changes are additive. Default CI schedule disabled for OSS forks; reporting pipeline is gated behind a feature flag and credentials.

Notes: kept runner interfaces backwards compatible with existing benchmark harness; most configuration is opt-in via benchmark-lab/configs/v140.yaml. See docs/benchmark-lab/README.md for runbook and sample outputs.
commits_summary: Add text_generation and embedding performance suites (suite configs and runners)
Introduce representative workload runners (chat/completions/embeddings/rerank) with distribution profiles
Add profiling baselines and harness for cold-start and steady-state measurements
Implement reporting pipeline: BigQuery uploader, summarizer, and DAG for nightly runs
Update CI: add benchmark workflow and guard flags
Fix flaky timing metric in runner harness and add additional logging
review_comments: Jordan Kim: Can we avoid the heavyweight BigQuery client on CI by using the stubbed uploader? Author: Yes — reporting is feature-flagged and CI uses the stub by default.
Avery Chen: The representative runner's backoff logic looked like it could skew tail-latency results. Author: tightened backoff windows and added a deterministic jitter seed for CI runs.
Samir Gupta: Please add a short runbook for incident response when nightly reporting fails. Author: added docs/benchmark-lab/README.md section and alerting playbook entry.
Jordan Kim: Approving pending one small nit on logging levels. Author: addressed — reduced noisy INFO logs in harness and pushed update.
CI Bot: benchmark-ci flaky on first run, rerun triggered and passed.
release_notes: Added benchmark-lab v140: new performance suites (text-generation, embeddings), representative workload runners, profiling baselines, and an opt-in reporting pipeline that publishes nightly summaries to BigQuery. Useful for detecting latency/cost regressions across model variants.
notes: This PR consolidates a set of internal tickets and replaces previous ad-hoc scripts with a unified harness. The reporting pipeline is behind a feature flag and requires credentials to enable uploads; default behavior writes local summaries for debugging.
merge_outcome: Merged to main via squash after reviews and CI passed. Nightly DAG staged to infra for rollout under feature flag.
